Maya (People Ops): heads-up — quick Q about timing for partial parental leave + intermittent remote work. manager asked whether someone can take 6 weeks at 60% capacity (3 days/week) instead of full-time leave. do we have a standard approach?
Ethan R: we had a case last quarter, i thought we allowed flexible schedules but payroll had to pro-rate benefits. what's the formal policy?
Maya (People Ops): we don't call out a single "60% leave" checkbox but we do support reduced-hours return or phased schedules. key points: need manager agreement, written plan in Workable/HR portal, and people-ops sign-off so payroll knows benefit pro-ration.
Sam: does this affect FMLA/CFRA eligibility or job protection windows? worried about inadvertently shortening protections.
Maya (People Ops): good call. intermittent leave can still be covered under FMLA/CFRA if they meet eligibility; the total protected time counts the same. we recommend documenting dates/hours so the legal leave clock is clear. People Ops can help draft the agreement template.
Ethan R: any required paperwork or fields we should include in the agreement?
Maya (People Ops): include: start/end dates, weekly expected hours, point of contact, how time off is requested, how coverage will be handled, whether PTO is used concurrently, and benefit status (full vs pro-rated). heres a minimal snippet to paste into the HR portal:
```
Parental Leave Plan - Phased Return
Employee: <name>
Start Date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
End Date (plan review): <YYYY-MM-DD>
Schedule: <e.g., 3 days/week, 8am-5pm>
Manager: <name>
Benefits: <full / pro-rated>
Notes: PTO concurrent use? <yes/no>
```
Sam: who actually approves benefit pro-ration? is it People Ops or Finance?
Finance Bot: Benefit proration approvals require People Ops + Payroll (Finance) sign-off for changes to deductions. Use the benefits change form: https://intranet.redwood/benefits/change-form
Ethan R: timeline for setup? team wants this to start next month. how long does payroll need?
Maya (People Ops): payroll needs benefit elections and signed agreement at least 2 payroll cycles prior to change. for EU/UK employees timelines may differ; work with local HR rep.
Sam: good to know. any tip for managers covering the 2 days gap each week?
Maya (People Ops): recommend documenting interim coverage (shared on-call, reduce deadlines, delegate reviews). People Ops can help with a manager checklist template. ill DM the template and pre-fill the HR portal entry if you share the employee name.
Ethan R: perfect, also will loop in Finance per the bots link. thanks Maya.
Maya (People Ops): np — ping if you want me to pre-approve before employee signs. :white_check_mark:
